activity_context.topic_title: Expected Values of Discrete Random Variables

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Expected Value Given the Frequency of a Random Variable
examples.problem:
Several children were asked about how many pets they have. The results were recorded below. If $X$ is the number of pets that a randomly selected child has, what is the expected value of $X?$

| Number of pets | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number of Children | $5$ | $6$ | $5$ |
examples.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\textrm E[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x \cdot f(x).
$$

We're given the frequencies of the number of pets, so we can start by computing the corresponding probabilities. The total number of children is $5+6+5=16,$ so the corresponding probabilities are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0)=f(0) & =\frac{5}{16} \\ P(X=1)=f(1) & =\frac{6}{16}=\frac{3}{8} \\ P(X=2)=f(2) & =\frac{5}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

We organize these results in the table below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\dfrac{5}{16}$ | $\dfrac{3}{8}$ | $\dfrac{5}{16}$ |

Now, summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2) \\  & =0(\frac{5}{16})+1(\frac{3}{8})+2(\frac{5}{16}) \\  & =0+\frac{3}{8}+\frac{10}{16} \\  & =0+\frac{6}{16}+\frac{10}{16} \\  & =\frac{0+6+10}{16} \\  & =\frac{16}{16} \\  & =1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
The total number of heads after $4$ flips of an unfair coin follows the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below. What is the expected value of the total number of heads after $4$ flips of the coin? Do not round the answer.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{3}{7}$ | $\frac{2}{7}$ | $\frac{1}{7}$ | $\frac{2}{21}$ | $\frac{1}{21}$ |

$\text{E}[X]=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4) \\  & =0(\frac{3}{7})+1(\frac{2}{7})+2(\frac{1}{7})+3(\frac{2}{21})+4(\frac{1}{21}) \\  & =0+\frac{2}{7}+\frac{2}{7}+\frac{6}{21}+\frac{4}{21} \\  & =0+\frac{6}{21}+\frac{6}{21}+\frac{6}{21}+\frac{4}{21} \\  & =\frac{0+6+6+6+4}{21} \\  & =\frac{22}{21}.\end{aligned}
$$
